title: How Beauteous Are Their Feet
description: How Beauteous Are Their Feet in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 10, headed “The blessedness of gospel times; or, The revelation of Christ to Jews and Gentiles, Isa. 5. 2 7-10. Matt. 13. 16 17”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How beau-teous are their feet Who stand on Zi-on's hill! Who bring sal-va-tion on their tongues, And words of peace re-veal!

lines: Who bring salvation on their tongues,
Which kings and prophets waited for,
Prophets and kings desir'd it long,
The Lord makes bare his arm

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
